# Settings reference

Every setting in **Extensions → Story Orchestrator**, by section. Each row says where the control is, what it does, when to change it and what it
costs, and its default. Settings apply to this whole install unless the control says "this chat". Rarely changed settings sit under their
section's **Advanced** fold.

## Playing

Which story this chat plays, and what you see while you play. [More](../player/playing.md)

| Setting | Where | What it does | Default | Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Notes under messages** | Settings › Playing › Notes under messages | Small icons under the replies: where the story moved, what it remembered, which lore it used. Story shows the basics and Behind the scenes a little more; neither shows spoilers. Off hides them. | 1 | `display.inline.level` |
| **Show this kind of note** | Settings › Playing › Notes under messages | Untick a kind of note to hide its icon under the messages. | Per entry | `display.inline.categories` |
| **Only the last … messages** | Settings › Playing › Notes under messages | Notes show under this many of the newest messages. Lower keeps long chats light. | 20 | `display.inline.window` |
| **Also post a chat note when the story moves on** | Settings › Playing › Also post a chat note | Posts a short note in the chat when the story reaches a new turning point. Off by default: the note sits after the reply and stops you swiping that reply. | Off | `display.announceTransitions` |
| **Show the story briefing when a story starts** | Settings › Playing › Show the story briefing | The first time a story starts in a chat, a page shows the author's briefing: the world, who you are, who is with you and how to play. You can re-open it from the drawer. | On | `display.briefing` |
| **Ask who you are when a story starts** | Settings › Playing › Ask who you are when a story starts | When a story says who you play, its start page asks once: keep, choose or create a persona. Off: your current one is kept. | On | `display.playerSetup` |
| **Mark story groups in the lists** | Settings › Playing › Mark story groups in the lists | A small icon beside each group, recent chat and past chat that plays a story. A saga, a story its author marks as one, gets its own icon. | On | `display.presence.listBadges` |
| **Your stories list** | Settings › Playing › Your stories list | Under Continue: the chats that play a story, newest first, with where each one is. One click opens the chat. | On | `display.presence.continueList` |
| **Story card on hover** | Settings › Playing › Story card on hover | Hovering or focusing a group's story icon shows the story, its chapter and when you last played it. | On | `display.presence.groupCard` |
| **Chapter title cards** | Settings › Playing › Chapter title cards | A full-width card under the message where a new chapter opens, instead of a small note. | On | `display.presence.chapterCard` |
| **Story entries in the wand menu** | Settings › Playing › Story entries in the wand menu | Story recap, the story briefing (when the story has one), flag this moment and the story drawer, from the extensions wand beside where you type. | On | `display.presence.wand` |
| **Dice chips under messages** | Settings › Playing › Dice chips under messages | A check a story makes public shows its roll under the message it decided ("Climb: 15 + 4 vs 12, success"). Author view also shows every other roll and background draw, here and in the Activity panel. | On | `display.presence.rollChips` |
| **Journal** | Story drawer › Journal | A movable panel with the story's quests: the main line you have reached, side quests and their steps, and a log of what happened. It shows only what you have found. | On | `display.presence.journal` |
| **Stat sheet** | Story drawer › Stat sheet | A movable panel with what the story keeps count of in the open: what you carry and the meters the author made public. | On | `display.presence.statSheet` |
| **Story panels** | Story drawer › Story panels | Extra panels a story adds, such as a clock that fills or a board of quests. Only what the author made public shows. | On | `display.presence.widgets` |
| **What could I do?** | Story drawer › What could I do? | A button in the story drawer and the wand menu that asks the memory model for a few things you could try next. A suggestion goes into the box where you type; nothing is sent until you send it. The request sees only what you have already seen in the story. | On | `display.presence.suggestions` |
| **Show story status above the chat input** | Settings › Playing › Show story status | A one-line strip above where you type: where the story is and how tense things are. Click it to open the story drawer. | On | `display.hudEnabled` |
| **Steer the tension** | Settings › Playing › Pacing | Adds a quiet note to the prompt that nudges the reply toward the story's intended tension: build it up, or let it cool down. | On | `pacing.hintEnabled` |

## Memory

The memory model that reads the chat, and what the story remembers. [More](../setup/memory-model.md)

| Setting | Where | What it does | Default | Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Let the story move forward on its own** | Settings › Memory › Memory model | After replies, a second model reads the chat and moves the story on when what it needs has happened. Leave it on unless you want to move the story by hand. Costs one call to the memory model every few messages. | On | `extraction.enabled` |
| **Memory model** | Settings › Memory › Memory model | The Connection Manager profile that reads the chat after replies to track the story and remember what happened. It does not replace your chat model. Pick a fast, cheap model; every chat uses this choice. | Not set | `extraction.profileId` |
| **Fallback when it is down** | Settings › Memory › Memory model | When the memory model stops answering, its work goes to this profile until it answers again; it is checked every few minutes and switched back on its own. Leave it empty and the work waits for the memory model. | None | `extraction.fallbackProfileId` |
| **Reply thinking** | Settings › Memory › Reply thinking | How long your chat model may think before each reply in a story chat. Medium is a good default: as clean as no limit, and replies start sooner. Only applies to llama.cpp setups that think; other backends are left alone. | Medium | `extraction.replyEffort` |
| **Read the chat every … messages** | Settings › Memory › Memory model | How often the memory model reads the chat. Lower reacts faster but calls the memory model more often; higher saves calls and reacts later. | 3 | `extraction.cadence` |
| **Wait before reading the newest messages** | Settings › Memory › Memory model | Leave the newest messages out of a read, in case you often re-roll them. 0 reacts to the newest message straight away; re-rolls are undone either way. | 0 | `extraction.stabilityLag` |
| **Model for this task** | Settings › Memory › Models per task | Send this task to a different Connection Manager profile than the memory model, for example a faster model for frequent work or a stronger one for summaries. Left on "Same as memory model", it uses the memory model. | Same as memory model | `extraction.profiles` |
| **Thinking for this task** | Settings › Memory › Models per task | How long the model may think on this task. Default sends nothing extra; higher can be more careful and costs time and tokens. | Per entry | `extraction.routes.*.route.options.effort` |
| **If the harness fails** | Settings › Memory › Models per task | What happens when the harness cannot answer: pause this task, or send it to a Connection Manager profile instead. | Per entry | `extraction.routes.*.onFailure.profileId` |
| **Show "Previously…" when a chat opens after a chapter ended** | Settings › Memory › Chapters | When you come back to a chat whose story finished a chapter, a short recap of that chapter is shown first. | On | `memory.chapters.recap` |
| **Write a record when a chapter ends** | Settings › Memory › Chapters | For stories that declare chapters: when a chapter ends, its memories are written up as one record. Costs a few memory model calls per chapter. | On | `memory.chapters.seal` |
| **Add the story so far to every prompt** | Settings › Memory › Chapters | The chapter records ride every prompt as a fixed-size story so far, so long stories keep their past. Uses the budget below. | On | `memory.chapters.storySoFar` |
| **Leave ended chapters' messages out of the prompt** | Settings › Memory › Chapters | Older chapters are represented by their record instead of their messages, which keeps prompts short in long stories. | On | `memory.chapters.fold` |
| **Story so far budget** | Settings › Memory › Chapters | How many tokens the story so far may take in each prompt. Larger keeps more of the past, and leaves less room for the chat. | 700 | `memory.chapters.chronicleTokens` |
| **Continuity warden** | Settings › Memory › Continuity warden | After each character reply, the judge checks it against the story's established facts; when it breaks one, the next reply's prompt restates that fact once. Needs the judge. Sends the reply, up to 40 facts and the tracked values. | On | `stagecraft.wardenEnabled` |
| **Warden notes** | Settings › Memory › Continuity warden | Ask me first: you approve each note. Add them on their own: notes go into the next prompt without you seeing them. | `review` | `stagecraft.wardenAcceptMode` |
| **Notes about the player's part** | Settings › Memory › Continuity warden | When a reply writes what only you do, say or decide, or ignores what you just said, the next reply's prompt carries a one-line reminder. Add them on their own (the default): the reminder goes in without anyone approving it. Ask me first: it waits like the other notes. Only replies are checked; your own messages are never changed. | `auto` | `stagecraft.agencyAcceptMode` |

## Characters

Who answers your messages in a group, and how many at once. [More](../author/topics/talk-control.md)

| Setting | Where | What it does | Default | Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Track what each character knows** | Settings › Memory › Advanced › Track what each character knows | The memory model also notes who knows what, and what each character is hiding, so characters do not know things they never saw. Turn it off when the self-test says this model cannot do it. | On | `memory.epistemicLedgerCapable` |
| **Read characters' reasoning for what they intend** | Settings › Characters › Inner voice | When a reply carries the character's reasoning, it is also read for what that character means to do. Needs knowledge tracking. Not measured yet. | On | `memory.harvestReasoning` |
| **Prepare a private inner beat for the next speaker** | Settings › Characters › Inner voice | After a reply, the memory model writes a short private note of what the likely next speaker wants, handed only to that character. At most two extra calls per turn, never while you wait for a reply. Not measured yet. | On | `memory.innerBeat` |
| **Inner beats for** | Settings › Characters › Inner voice | Prepare the beat for the likeliest speaker only, or for the two likeliest. Two costs one more call per turn. | Next speaker only | `memory.innerFanOut` |
| **Speaker direction in group chats** | Story drawer › Overview › Chat preferences | In a group chat, the story picks the character the scene calls for instead of rotating through everyone. This switch is for this chat only. | On | `talk.enabled` |
| **Several characters may answer one message** | Settings › Characters › Speaker direction | In a group chat, more than one character can reply to a single message; the story picks each next speaker and stops when it is your turn. Off: one voice per turn. | On | `talk.chain.enabled` |
| **Voices per turn at most** | Settings › Characters › Speaker direction | The most characters that may answer one of your messages. Higher makes busier scenes and longer waits. | 3 | `talk.chain.max` |

## World

How a story's lorebooks are switched on, and the lorebook helper. [More](../author/topics/world-info.md)

| Setting | Where | What it does | Default | Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **How story lorebook entries switch on** | Settings › World › Lorebooks | Per chat (the default): entries rest off in their lorebook files and each chat sees its own story's entries switched on. File writes: entries are switched on and off in their lorebook files as a chat moves. | `scan` | `worldInfo.gatingMode` |
| **Memory text can trigger lore** | Settings › World › Lorebooks | Established facts, scene history and the current guidance join every lorebook scan, so an entry whose keys they mention can activate. What characters privately know never joins it. | On | `worldInfo.scanMemory` |
| **Lorebook curator** | Settings › World › Background helpers | A background helper that reads what has happened and proposes changes to the story's own lorebook. It only touches the lorebooks the story lists, proposes rather than writes, and never changes story progress or memory. | On | `stagecraft.curatorEnabled` |
| **Curator changes** | Settings › World › Background helpers | Ask me first: you approve each change. Apply on their own: changes to entries marked {{// so:auto}} land at the next reply, the rest still wait for you. Never apply: only show what it would do. | `review` | `stagecraft.acceptMode` |
| **Off-stage events** | Settings › World › Background helpers | For stories whose characters have plans: when the story moves on or a scene ends, the memory model proposes one short thing a character did off stage toward that plan. Each one waits for you in Author view and, once accepted, reaches only that character at the next reply. Do not propose: no calls are made. | `review` | `stagecraft.meanwhileAcceptMode` |

## Images

Optional pictures and character sprites; both need your own image setup. [More](../setup/images.md)

| Setting | Where | What it does | Default | Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Allow automatic illustrations on this install** | Settings › Images › Image service | Lets stories and the automation below draw pictures through SillyTavern’s configured image backend. An image-prompt model is optional; without one, a template uses the current scene. | On | `image.enabled` |
| **Image backend** | Settings › Images › Image service | Use SillyTavern’s configured Image Generation service, or advanced ComfyUI recipes through the optional media plugin. | `st` | `image.backend` |
| **When pictures are drawn** | Settings › Images › Image service | Story: at the moments each story asks for. Every N: every few replies, plus those moments. Model requests: when the model asks. Manual: only when you ask. | `story` | `image.automation.mode` |
| **Every N replies** | Settings › Images › Image service | Draw a picture every this many replies. Lower draws more often and keeps the GPU busier. | 5 | `image.automation.everyN` |
| **Image-prompt model** | Settings › Images › Image service | The Connection Manager profile that turns the scene and the story's visual direction into a picture prompt. Separate from the chat model. | Not set | `image.directorProfileId` |
| **ComfyUI address** | Settings › Images › Image service | Where your ComfyUI server listens. When text and image models share a GPU, use the GPU broker for your text profiles. | Not set | `image.comfyUrl` |
| **Avoid explicit imagery** | Settings › Images › Image service | Adds safety terms to every picture prompt and skips explicit requests. | Off | `image.safeMode` |
| **Model** | Settings › Images › Image service | The ComfyUI model this kind of picture uses. Left on automatic, it uses the one installed model of the recipe family; with none or several, Setup asks you to choose. | Per entry | `image.purposes.*.checkpoint` |
| **Recipe family** | Settings › Images › Image service | Choose the workflow family supported by your installed checkpoint. A file name alone does not identify its architecture. | Per entry | `image.purposes.*.family` |
| **Quality** | Settings › Images › Image service | Base is faster; hires adds an upscale pass and takes longer. | Per entry | `image.purposes.*.quality` |
| **Shape** | Settings › Images › Image service | The picture's proportions. Auto lets the image-prompt model choose. | Per entry | `image.purposes.*.aspect` |
| **Framing** | Settings › Images › Image service | How close the camera is: from a close-up to a wide view. | Per entry | `image.purposes.*.shot` |
| **Where it appears** | Settings › Images › Image service | In the message, as its own message, or as the chat background. | Per entry | `image.purposes.*.placement` |
| **Pictures to choose from** | Settings › Images › Image service | Draw this many and keep the best. Each extra one costs another render. | Per entry | `image.purposes.*.candidates` |
| **Let the image-prompt model pick another model** | Settings › Images › Image service | The image-prompt model may switch this picture to a different image model when it fits better. | Per entry | `image.purposes.*.directorMayOverride` |
| **Always add** | Settings › Images › Image service | Words added to every prompt of this kind. | Per entry | `image.purposes.*.extraPositive` |
| **Always avoid** | Settings › Images › Image service | Words added to the avoid list of every prompt of this kind. | Per entry | `image.purposes.*.extraNegative` |
| **Fixed look** | Settings › Images › Image service | Image tags that describe this character, used when the story has not described them. | Per entry | `image.characters.*.appearanceTags` |
| **Always include** | Settings › Images › Image service | Tags added to every picture of this character. | Per entry | `image.characters.*.alwaysTags` |
| **Never include** | Settings › Images › Image service | Tags kept out of every picture of this character. | Per entry | `image.characters.*.neverTags` |
| **Show character sprites that change expression as replies stream** | Settings › Images › Sprite stage | Shows the speaking characters on a small stage, and changes their expression with the reply. Needs a sprite pack for each character. | Off | `sprites.enabled` |
| **Show the stage** | Settings › Images › Sprite stage | With Visual Novel mode: only while SillyTavern's /vn mode is on. Always: in every chat that has sprites. | `vn` | `sprites.stage` |
| **Expression model when the judge is off** | Settings › Images › Sprite stage | Which profile picks expressions when the judge cannot. Same as the image-prompt model by default. | Not set | `sprites.profileId` |
| **Dim whoever is not speaking** | Settings › Images › Sprite stage | Fades the characters who are not talking, so the speaker stands out. | On | `sprites.focus` |
| **Idle breathing** | Settings › Images › Sprite stage | A slow, small movement so sprites do not look frozen. Turn it off to save a little work on slow machines. | On | `sprites.breathing` |
| **Blink** | Settings › Images › Sprite stage | Uses eyes-closed frames when the sprite pack has them. Reduced motion switches this off. | On | `sprites.blink` |
| **Current character state in replies** | Settings › Images › Sprite stage | Adds this story’s applied public changes to the next reply prompt. Character cards and personas stay unchanged. | On | `sprites.cardOverlay` |
| **Generate changed looks when needed** | Settings › Images › Sprite stage | Uses the Studio builder’s saved reference setup to edit the current expression when a public look changes. Needs the media plugin and ComfyUI. The current sprite stays visible while rendering. | On | `sprites.onDemand` |
| **Mouth movement** | Settings › Images › Sprite stage | Moves the speaking character’s mouth while replies stream. Simple, the default, switches between closed and open frames. Smooth adds half-open frames when the pack has them. Reduced motion switches this off. | `simple` | `sprites.mouth` |
| **Render preset** | Settings › Images › Sprite stage | The size and steps the Studio sprite builder starts with. Standard renders at 1024 px with 25 steps; Fast preview at 512 px with 20 steps, quicker but softer. | `standard` | `sprites.renderPreset` |

## Judge

An optional fast model for small choices; it never blocks a reply. [More](../setup/judge.md)

| Setting | Where | What it does | Default | Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Use the judge** | Settings › Judge | A second, fast model for yes/no and pick-one decisions. Each use can be switched off on its own and says what it sends. It never receives character cards, persona text, other chats or the key. | On | `judge.enabled` |
| **Judge uses** | Settings › Judge | Each use answers one kind of question for the story. Switch off any you do not want; the story falls back to its usual path. | Per entry | `judge.uses` |
| **Where this use runs** | Settings › Judge | Which provider answers this use. A provider that was not measured for a use is refused, and the use takes its usual path. | Per entry | `judge.provider` |

## Authoring

Tools for writing stories. [More](../author/README.md)

| Setting | Where | What it does | Default | Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Enable the wizard** | Settings › Start › New story | Turns on the story wizard in the Studio and the author's suggestion tools. It uses your authoring model and costs calls only while you use it. | On | `copilot.enabled` |
| **Outlines per gap** | Settings › Judge › Outlines for the road ahead | Write this many outlines for each gap in the story and keep the best one. Each extra outline is another run of the story model. | 1 | `judge.expansion.variants` |
| **Best outline picked by** | Settings › Judge › Outlines for the road ahead | Who picks the best outline: the judge's score, or the story model. | `code` | `judge.expansion.pick` |
